With DoD/VA, cash discounts and possibly price protection all in the same line, and no 340B split disclosed, no sized number backs the 340B claim.

round2.conceded: Peer-wide realized-tense wording (MRK, AMGN) and the possible price-protection content of charge-backs. Together these mean the 340B dollar effect cannot be isolated, so I move from held/minor to refuted.
round2.held: The arithmetic is correct and the reader labelled it an upper bound, so this is not a math error; c01 and c02 still overlap and cannot be added.
round2.narrowed: From 'up to $1.9B of 340B drag' to 'charge-backs explain ~78% of the 2025 GTN-rate rise; 340B share unsized'.

verdicts.argument: Both skeptics independently read the grade-B Lenkowsky remark (BMY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p1) as a revenue and phasing statement, not a GTN-rate statement, so the contradiction does not hold. My line-item point stands: on BMY:10k_FY2025.md p49, Medicaid and Medicare rebates were only ~$0.59B above the 2024 rate.

verdicts.argument: I checked their sources. The diabetes expiry is guided: 2025Q4 call (grade C) 'OI and E expense of approximately $700 million, which reflects the expiry of our royalty-bearing license of diabetes products'; Q2 2026 release p3 repeats it; FY2023 10-K p32 and FY2024 10-K p33 carry the Keytruda/Tecentriq 2026-12-31 end almost verbatim. I concede all of that. On the narrowed 2027 piece, it is material. H1 2026 Keytruda 308 + Tecentriq 26 = 334 (10-Q p10), so about $0.62-0.67B pretax a year (FY2025 actual 588 + 47 = 635, 10-K p91). After tax at the ~18% guided rate (release p6), 668 x 0.82 / 2,039 = $0.27, which is 4.1% of the FY2027 I/B/E/S mean of $6.54 and 3.6% of FY2027 consensus pretax $18,488M (ibes rows #510, #1674). That clears the 'few cents of EPS' bar easily. Is it visibly in consensus? No, and it cannot be shown either way. FY2027 vs FY2026 consensus is EPS -$0.34 (6.54 vs 6.88) and pretax -$396M (18,488 vs 18,884). That decline must also absorb management's $1.5-2B 2027 Eliquis step-down (2026Q2 call, grade C), and the royalty alone ($0.67B) is larger than the whole pretax decline. So consensus assumes offsetting growth, and I/B/E/S has no OI&E line to show whether the royalty was removed. The Q4 2025 release p14 folds Keytruda and Tecentriq into 'Royalty and licensing income (1,093)' with other items, so the stream is not a visible line in the releases investors model. Only 10-K/10-Q Note 4 splits it out. The 2027 EPS dispersion (stdev $0.44, high $7.63) is wider than the effect, which fits some models not having it. Caveat: the I/B/E/S rows are verify_status no_verified_copy (WRDS licensed), so they support the argument but should not be quoted publicly.
verdicts.correction: Keytruda and Tecentriq royalties of ~$0.62-0.67B pretax (~$0.27 EPS, ~4% of FY2027 consensus EPS) stop on 2026-12-31. They appear only as Note 4 lines, not in the release P&L, and no 2025Q3-2026Q2 call mentions them. Consensus FY2027 pretax falls only $0.40B while also absorbing a guided $1.5-2B Eliquis step-down, so whether the street has removed the royalty cannot be confirmed. Drop the diabetes piece and the $1.76B total.

round2.conceded: The diabetes expiry is guided and in releases, and the end dates have been in Item 1A since FY2023. The 'in footnotes, not in tables investors model' framing is wrong for diabetes, and the $1.76B headline should go.
round2.held: The 2027 Keytruda/Tecentriq piece is material (~4% of FY2027 EPS, 3.6% of pretax). It is not broken out in the releases (they show a combined royalty-and-licensing line), and none of the four latest calls mentions it.
round2.narrowed: From a $1.76B three-stream cliff to a $0.62-0.67B 2027-only cliff. 'Not priced' becomes 'not visibly priced': consensus cannot be decomposed to show it.

verdicts.argument: Their grade-C call evidence (2025Q4: the ~40% WAC cut 'eliminates inflationary penalties or CPI penalties of statutory rebates', confirmed in the 2025Q4 transcript p1 summary text) shows management stated the mechanism plainly. My math objection is independent and stands: the $2,757M rebate drop is offset by a $4,002M gross decline (10-Q p31), and Eliquis rose only $801M in Q2 (10-Q p8), which the 10-Q p35 attributes first to demand.
verdicts.correction: Only their suggested materiality test survives: whether the size of the 2026 rebate reset implies a 2027 step-down larger than the guided $1.5-2B. Nothing in the sources sizes that, so it is a lead, not a finding.

round2.conceded: Obviousness is fatal on its own: the mechanism was explained on three calls.
round2.held: The level-vs-offset math error (a deduction-line drop treated as upside) and the demand-first attribution.
round2.narrowed: Severity raised from major to fatal once obviousness is added; no remaining claim.

verdicts.argument: Both skeptics agree. Their 2026Q1 cash-collection quote ($1.2B lower collections from the list cut, grade C) fits my reading that the reserve build is the balance-sheet side of the GTN already counted.
verdicts.correction: Footnote to the Eliquis price-reset story at most.

round2.conceded: Their price-protection reading of the $820M reserve rise is more specific than mine.

verdicts.argument: Both skeptics agree. The release footnote change they cite (release p2) makes it visible as well as immaterial (0.9% of revenue, BMY:10k_FY2025.md p85).

round2.conceded: It is also printed in the earnings-release footnote, not only the 10-Q.

verdicts.argument: Can it be a finding under the citation rules? Yes, but only as fact-row numbers. BLIND_READER_BRIEF rule 4 allows numbers from 'a page or fact row you cite', and data/moat/verified/ is an allowed source. pricing/gtn_proxy.csv#40 and #155 sit in doc pricing:verified/pricing/gtn_proxy.csv with verify_status 'verified'. The HELPERS.md machine-data ban covers the unverified_raw kinds (raw nadac, wac_event, partd_support, partb_asp), not this verified derived table. So I narrow my round-1 claim: the 1.36x and 2.83x ratios and the $313/$558 30-day NADAC medians can be cited by fact locator. They cannot be quoted as text, and the underlying raw NADAC must not be deep-linked. The only quotable page is the CMS fact sheet p2 (MFP $231 vs $197; 2023 list $521 vs $517). Row #155's own basis note says the Xarelto NADAC mixes EA/ML NDCs and the ratio uses EA NDCs only, so that caveat must travel with the number. On materiality the original candidate still fails. 'About 44% cheaper in every non-Medicare channel' is a list or acquisition-cost gap, not a net gap (Medicaid gets Eliquis free per the press release p1, and commercial rebates are confidential). The tie to 27% U.S. growth is contradicted by the 10-Q p35 attribution to demand, and by management's share-gain story (2026Q2 call, grade C, 'new-to-brand share approaching 80%').
verdicts.correction: Allowed, narrowed version (agreeing with the obviousness skeptic's correction): after the 2026 list cut, Eliquis's pharmacy acquisition cost is ~1.36x its Medicare negotiated price vs ~2.83x for Xarelto (verified fact rows #40 and #155, EA NDCs, cite by locator, no quote). Both had near-equal 2023 list prices (CMS p2). State it as a list-level peer contrast with no revenue or share sizing. As written, it is not a material finding with a number an investor can model.

round2.conceded: In round 1 I implied the NADAC ratios could not be used. They come from a verified derived table that rule 4 allows as a cited fact row, so c07 is citable. The obviousness skeptic is right that nobody has set the two gaps side by side.
round2.held: The original claim (44% cheaper in every non-Medicare channel; causal link to growth) is a list-vs-net error and unsized, so it stays refuted on materiality.
round2.narrowed: From 'cannot be quoted' to: citable by fact locator only, no text quote, carry the EA-NDC caveat, present as a qualitative list-level contrast.

verdicts.argument: Their evidence that the renal/dialysis text is long-standing on the label, and that management itself names renal-impairment patients in the milvexian pitch (2026Q2 call p1, grade C, confirmed: 'patients who have renal impairment'), combines with my point that nothing is sized and the dialysis subgroup cannot explain a 2.6M-enrollee gap.
verdicts.correction: Drop as a finding. The milvexian label-match question is a lead with no testable number yet.

round2.conceded: The label fact is old and management already discusses the renal group, so I move from held to refuted.

verdicts.argument: On materiality, Eliquis is the right-size product (30% of 2025 revenue, release p6). The obviousness skeptic's objection is that every team picks it, which is not a materiality defect. I agree the fine-print edge should move from the renal label (obvious, unsized) to the c07 list-to-MFP contrast, cited by fact locator.
verdicts.correction: Keep Eliquis vs Xarelto; use the c07 narrowed contrast as the fine-print edge, with the EA-NDC caveat and no net-price claim.

round2.conceded: Eliquis is obvious as a pick, and the label edge is weak.
round2.held: The pick is material and the pair lines up cleanly.
round2.narrowed: Fine-print edge switched to the c07 contrast.

overall: After both lenses, the only material, citable and not-plainly-stated item is the 2027 end of the Keytruda/Tecentriq royalties (~$0.62-0.67B pretax, ~$0.27 or ~4% of FY2027 consensus EPS). It is absent from release lines and recent calls, and consensus cannot be decomposed to show it is priced. The Eliquis vs Xarelto list-to-MFP contrast (c07) is citable by verified fact locator, but only as an unsized list-level contrast. Everything else is obvious, double-counted or below the materiality bar.
